title: The Yellow Card (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational soccer philosophy 104bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal absurdist sport football
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The yellow card is produced from the breast pocket of the man
Who has decided that your contribution to this plan
Was slightly over the acceptable and needs to be addressed
By a rectangle of laminated yellow — you're assessed

[Pre-Chorus]
I once got a yellow card in a five-a-side on a Thursday night
For arguing with the volunteer referee about a call that wasn't right

[Chorus]
The yellow card says something nobody needs to say
You've been noted and recorded and it doesn't go away
The yellow card is official now — it's in the book and done
You have one more before the red and then you're gone, son
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
The player always responds by looking at his boots
As if the boots explain the tackle that the referee disputes
Sometimes the hands go up in the gesture of the wrongly done
But the card is out, the notebook's closed — the conversation's won

[Bridge]
I have given out yellow cards in my life that weren't actual cards
They were looks across a dinner table at a man who dropped his guard
The rectangle of disapproval needs no laminate to work
It works in kitchens too, and hallways, and wherever
The yellow card is universal

[Outro]
Yellow card knows… noted and recorded… yellow card knows
That's my boy
